function: Distributed MADRL agents, one per BS, jointly select BS-UE association, number of streams and codebook RF beams (hybrid beamforming) to maximize the effective sum rate (p. 6-8)
system: Downlink cell-free: I BSs (36 antennas), K UEs (16 antennas), hybrid beamforming, 4 RF chains each; no RIS; 100 GHz, 120 MHz bandwidth (p. 3, p. 10)
method: Distributed multi-agent deep RL: per-BS actor-critic agents with entropy term, one-hot action picking one beam tuple per timestep; trained before each coherence block (p. 3, 8-9)
data_channel: Custom simulator: sub-THz channel with probabilistic LOS plus Np=4 NLOS paths, angle and gain distributions from 3GPP study [25]; PPP-placed BSs and UEs (p. 3, p. 10)
test_conditions: Random PPP topologies re-drawn per run; sweeps over I=K (5-35), Nc, coherence time, UE position error, transmit power; no unseen-configuration test stated (p. 10-15)
baselines: Non-learned: HBF [3], FP-based DBF [12], beam-domain DBF and HBF [13], SLSQP bound. Learned: MADDPG [44], MATD3 [45], and own variants (single action, centralized critic) (p. 10-14)
metrics: Achievable sum rate, signaling overhead, episode reward, execution time, sum-rate ratio to SLSQP bound; scalability with I and K (p. 11-15)
complexity: Big-O complexity per method in Table III, independent of I and K for the proposed method (p. 14-15); execution time about 1371 times below SLSQP (p. 13)
q1_support: p. 4: channel angles and gains follow "the angle distribution and the gain distribution in [25]"; p. 16: [25] is "Study on Channel Model for Frequencies From 0.5 to 100 GHz Version 16.1.0, ETSI 3GPP".
q2_support: p. 3: "Before transmitting the data during each channel coherence time" a training phase runs; p. 10: "When the simulation is re-run" topologies are redrawn. Missing: any trained agent tested with other I, K, antennas, band or channel model.
q3_support: p. 11: "MADDPG- and MATD3-based Link Configurations" as learned baselines; p. 12: "In Fig. 4(b), MADDPG and MATD3 achieve lower sum rate compared to the proposed method" and "the proposed method obtains 5.55% higher sum rate compared to [13]" (non-learned).
q4_support: p. 14: "the computational complexity of the different link configuration methods is presented" in Table III (p. 15); p. 13: "requiring approximately 1371 times less execution time" than SLSQP.
q5_support: p. 10: "At the beginning of each simulation, the BSs and UEs are randomly distributed within the specified region"; the data are self-simulated. Missing: any code or data link, and any public dataset or measured data.
notes: Area 3: the learned element selects RF beams from DFT codebooks together with BS-UE association and stream numbers; baseband BF is a closed-form SLNR design (p. 5), so the above-PHY check passes because association is learned jointly with beam selection. q1 borderline: the paper cites [25] without writing TR 38.901; by its title [25] is the 3GPP TR 38.901 study, and the LOS probability and CI path-loss exponents 2.1 and 3.19 (p. 3) look like its UMi model, an identification made by the assistant, in an own simplified simulator. q2: learning runs per channel realization and no trained agent is applied to another setting. q3: Single Action and centralized-critic are variants of the proposed method and are not counted. Tables II-III and Figs. 4-11 were read as page images (p. 10, 12, 14, 15).
